scope.applicability: Versioned semantic artifacts whose normative meaning may change independently of representation.
exclusions: Schema-only or encoding-only changes preserving meaning.
Lifecycle labels inferred from filesystem paths.

scientific_formal.normative_statement: A Semantic Epoch is one immutable owner-selected version of an artifact's normative meaning. A successor Semantic Epoch is required exactly when the owner determines that the artifact's identity-preserving normative meaning, scope, exclusions, owned model, or semantic contracts materially changed. Representation-only revisions and derived refreshes do not create Semantic Epochs.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: NewSemanticEpoch(a_before,a_after) iff MaterialNormativeMeaning(a_before) != MaterialNormativeMeaning(a_after). RepresentationChanged and MeaningEqual does not imply NewSemanticEpoch.
boundary_conditions: A byte change alone does not prove semantic change.
A claim that meaning is preserved is reviewable evidence, not automatic equivalence.
A semantic successor requires explicit owner selection and applicable lineage.
testable_conditions: The change assessment separates semantic fields from representation fields.
Every new epoch identifies its predecessor and material meaning delta.
No representation-only change is classified as semantic lineage.

plain_language.explanation: A new chapter of meaning. It is created because what the artifact means changed, not merely because its JSON shape or generated documentation changed.

domain_context.explanation: A Governance context needs a new Semantic Epoch when its owned model or scope changes. Removing a redundant Context Map backreference while preserving that meaning should not produce a context v3 epoch.
examples: Changing a Bounded Context's owned domain model is a semantic-epoch candidate.
Re-encoding the same context under Bounded Context/v2 is not, by itself, a semantic epoch.

boundaries: Semantic Epoch is not Representation Revision.
Semantic Epoch is not a generator version or schema revision.
Filesystem version labels cannot establish semantic succession by themselves.
claim_ceiling: This candidate defines semantic versioning meaning only. It does not classify any existing artifact, create lineage, or select a successor.
